ov: The vast majority of the insect order that also includes butterflies, with about 160,000 species. Most fly at night, and only the caterpillars of a few species eat clothes.

why.et: Some caterpillars, the larvae of moths and butterflies, are eaten by people.
why.ac: Most moths are nocturnal, though some fly at dusk or by day.

rg: Every continent except Antarctica, across a huge range of land habitats.
df: Caterpillars mostly eat plants. Some adults don’t eat at all.

cf.tip: Butterflies fly by day, have clubbed antennae and rest with wings held upright. Most moths fly at night, have feathery or tapering antennae, and rest with wings flat.

fx: Nobody knows for sure why moths circle lights. One idea is that they steer by the moon, and a lamp confuses them.
